title: Oscar and the Scholarship
premise: Oscar Vasquez, a scholarship student at Ashgrove Academy, has survived on silence: about the money, the dead-end neighborhood he hides from classmates, and the night his brother was arrested for a crime Oscar witnessed but never reported. When a college essay prompt — 'Describe a moment you chose not to act' — forces him to write the truth, his draft leaks, and the academy's powerful donors close ranks to protect their own son, the real culprit. With help from three unlikely friends who become his found family, Oscar chooses justice outside the law, exposing the cover-up through the final spring audition itself. He loses the scholarship's patronage and nearly loses his best friend, but gains a truth that sets them all free.
about_author: Xanthe Lockridge is the pen name of a former admissions counselor who spent a decade reading essays she suspected were lies. She writes young adult fiction about kids who are 'fine' and the cost of pretending.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A tour-guide-perfect day at Ashgrove: Oscar charms visiting families, hides his patched uniform, and deflects his roommate Theo's questions about winter break. Emotional beat: polished performance masking exhaustion; readers see the first hairline crack when he flinches at a police siren.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. English teacher Ms. Okafor assigns the common app prompt: describe a moment you chose not to act. Oscar freezes, then writes three brutal pages about the alley behind Delgado's market — then deletes it and submits something safe. Beat: dread; the deleted draft saved in a folder titled 'trash.'

chapters.title: Marguerite Knows
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The other scholarship kid, sharp-tongued Marguerite, catches Oscar re-reading the deleted draft in the library and recognizes the look of someone carrying a body. She shares her own secret — an undocumented mother — as collateral trust. Beat: wary kinship between two people fluent in hiding.

chapters.title: The Wrong Brother
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Flashback woven into present: two years ago, Oscar watched Marcus Hale — donor-son, Ashgrove golden boy — start the fire that got Oscar's brother Rafa arrested for arson. He told no one. Present-day Marcus greets him warmly at a fundraiser. Beat: nausea of complicity.

chapters.title: Sync Error
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finds the 'trash' folder while borrowing Oscar's laptop for a film project. He reads it, says nothing, and starts acting strange — protective, guilty. Beat: dramatic irony; friendship strained by an unspoken burden.

chapters.title: Scholarship Review
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Headmaster Whitlock announces mid-year 'scholarship reviews' — thinly veiled pressure on financial aid students after a donor complaint. Marguerite suspects Marcus's father is behind it. Beat: institutional menace made personal.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The deleted draft surfaces anonymously on the school gossip account, redacted but recognizable. Whispers follow Oscar through hallways; Marcus's smile tightens. Beat: exposure terror — the thing he wrote to survive now hunts him.

chapters.title: Deniability
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV (first antagonist chapter). Marcus privately offers Oscar a paid internship and a quiet NDA, framing it as generosity. He reveals he knows about Rafa's parole hearing date. Beat: velvet threat; Oscar realizes how much power they hold.

chapters.title: Found Family, Improvised
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite, Theo, and debate-team outsider Priya convene an emergency meeting in the boiler room, formally declaring themselves Oscar's people whether he likes it or not. Beat: warmth breaking through fear — the found family forms.

chapters.title: Rafa's Hearing
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar attends Rafa's parole hearing and watches the Hales' lawyer bury the board in technicalities. Rafa, dignified, tells Oscar not to burn his life down for him. Beat: heartbreak; the legal system fails exactly as designed.

chapters.title: What Priya Found
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya discovers the academy's insurance records list a second fire report naming Marcus, sealed by Whitlock. Proof exists — if anyone can get it out without being expelled or sued. Beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: The Offer Oscar Refuses
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Whitlock offers Oscar full ride through college plus expunged records for Rafa — in exchange for recanting. For one long scene, Oscar genuinely considers it. Beat: temptation; survival versus soul.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confronts Oscar: why did you let me read it and say nothing? Why did you let Rafa rot? Their fight turns cruel and true. Beat: the found family's first real wound; Theo walks out.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Gamble
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. To shield Oscar, Marguerite claims authorship of the leaked essay — risking her own scholarship review. Oscar must decide whether to let her take the fall. Beat: sacrifice offered; Oscar refuses to be protected by silence again.

chapters.title: Spring Audition
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Setup: the annual arts showcase doubles as the scholarship showcase before donors, including old man Hale. Oscar, a cellist, is slotted last. He and his friends plan to turn the performance into testimony. Beat: coiled anticipation.

chapters.title: Interference
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus, rattled, escalates: an anonymous tip gets Priya suspended, and Theo's college recommendation mysteriously vanishes. Marcus believes he's protecting himself but we glimpse his own fear of his father. Beat: antagonist under pressure, doubling down.

chapters.title: Rehearsal in the Dark
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The four regroup in the theater overnight — Theo returns, unasked, with coffee and the missing recommendation letter he'd stolen back. They rehearse the plan: Oscar will play, then speak. Beat: reconciliation; family rebuilt stronger.

chapters.title: The Audition
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Climax part one: Oscar performs a piece built from Rafa's voicemails, then reads the essay aloud, unredacted, to a stunned auditorium including the Hales. Security moves in; Marguerite stands, then Theo, then half the student body. Beat: catharsis through public truth.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Immediate
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Chaos: donors threaten lawsuits, Whitlock suspends Oscar pending expulsion, but the recording is already everywhere. A local journalist calls the sealed fire report 'newsworthy.' Beat: vertigo between ruin and vindication.

chapters.title: Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The Hales' lawyer offers one final deal; Oscar declines on record. Instead, the friends deliver copies of the evidence to the district attorney, a reporter, and Rafa's public defender simultaneously — justice by distribution, not permission. Beat: agency reclaimed.

chapters.title: What the Truth Cost
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Fallout settles: Marcus withdraws from Ashgrove; Whitlock resigns; Oscar is reinstated but loses the endowed scholarship and must leave the school. Rafa's case is reopened. Beat: bittersweet accounting — every gain itemized against its price.

chapters.title: The Essay That Mattered
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, epilogue. At his new public school, Oscar submits his real college essay — the same one, unchanged. Marguerite visits with news of her own acceptance; Theo films everything. Final beat: 'I'm not fine,' he writes. 'That's how I know I'm going to be.'
